title: Customer Admin Guide — Build a Winning Proposal

lede: The customer's eight-step journey through the govwin proposal portal — from a ranked opportunity to a submission-ready, downloadable proposal.
Every step below was verified on a real effort: the Immobileyes NAVAIR/NAVSEA Counter-UAS SBIR (topic DON26BX03-NP002). The screenshots are that live run.
hero.badge: Verified end-to-end · every step through the platform's real tools & agents

footer: govwin — RFP Pipeline Portal · Customer Admin role. Under-the-hood references (routes, tools, cores) are shown so the guide doubles as living documentation. Companion guides: RFP-Admin Operations, Collaborator.

sections.heading: Sign in & your portal
sections.body: Sign in with the credentials your RFP-Pipeline admin issued. Your dashboard is role-aware: it opens on your company's workspace and surfaces your live ToDos — opportunities to review, proposals in progress, and anything waiting on you.
sections.caption: The customer-admin landing: your workspace + role-aware ToDos.

sections.heading: Find your opportunity (ranked cards)
body: The Opportunity Pipeline shows every opportunity the platform has pushed to you, ranked by your Spotlight buckets. Each card carries the agency, program, and close date. Pin copies the solicitation's documents into your workspace; Build opens the proposal workspace.
In the verified run, the NAVAIR/NAVSEA Counter-UAS topic DON26BX03-NP002 ranks #1 for Immobileyes — the best fit for a counter-drone optics company.
sections.caption: The DON26BX03-NP002 C-UAS card ranked #1 in the Immobileyes pipeline.

sections.heading: Set your scoring criteria (buckets)
sections.body: Spotlight buckets are your scoring criteria — the themes you care about (e.g. “Counter-UAS”, “AI sensor fusion”). Every card is scored against each bucket, and editing a bucket re-ranks your pipeline automatically. This is deterministic today; an optional scoring agent overlays it later.
sections.caption: Buckets define what ranks to the top of your pipeline.

sections.heading: Build your content library (upload → atomize)
body: Your library is the raw material every draft is built from. On Library → Upload package, drop your past proposals, capability docs, résumés, and data (PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX). The atomizer deconstructs each file into a reference atom (the whole doc) plus one primitive atom per substantive block, and auto-tags them against the shared taxonomy (volume, kind, agency, program, phase).

Verified: five Immobileyes documents (GHOST draft, TACFI Technical Volume, résumés, foreign affiliations, cost proposal) atomized into 24 atoms — tagged vol:technical vol:cost vol:key_personnel kind:bio and more. Each uploaded package also gets a “Save as template” button (templify) to reuse its winning structure.
sections.caption: The real atomizer: 24 tagged atoms from five uploaded Immobileyes documents.

sections.heading: Group atoms & arrange the canvas
body: Atoms aren't just a flat list. In the library, select several primitives and Group into new atom to compose a reusable bundle — a “Team for Navy” group, a past-performance set. Inside a section, “+ From Library” inserts atoms straight into the canvas as nodes, and you drag to reorder them into the flow you want.
Verified: three GHOST past-performance & partner primitives composed into one group, inserted into the Related Work section, then reordered on the canvas.
sections.caption: Composing primitives into a reusable group in the library.

sections.heading: Open the proposal & compliance matrix
body: Opening a proposal provisions the full compliance matrix — every required volume and item the solicitation demands, each linked to a section “mold” that carries the format rules (page limit, margins, font). The specific agency template is built into the matrix, so the structure is correct before you write a word.
Verified: the DON 6-volume CSO structure (Cover · Technical · Cost · CCR · Supporting · FWA), with Volume 2 aligned to the DON Phase-I Open-Topic Technical Volume 2 template (8 sections).
sections.caption: The 6-volume matrix; Volume 2 aligned to the DON TV2 template, ready to draft.

sections.heading: Draft each section with the AI agent
body: Open a section and click Draft (or Draft all sections). The drafting agent reads the RFP context and the section's compliance mold, pulls the most relevant atoms from your library, and writes canvas content sized to the page budget — you review, pick atoms, and revise in the canvas editor. Nothing auto-commits: it's advisory until you accept.
Verified: the proposal.draft_section agent tool ran on all 8 Technical-Volume sections, grounded in the atomized library, applying its budget/fit check (≈ a 2-page, ~1,090-word target per section).
sections.caption: The canvas editor — draft, pick atoms, and revise each section.

sections.heading: Accept & Lock → the matrix turns green
body: When a section is right, Accept & Lock it. Locking flips its compliance row to “satisfied,” snapshots the version, harvests reusable content back into your library, and rolls the volume up. When every section of a volume is locked, the volume shows ✓ Volume locked and downloads unlock.
Verified: locking via lockSectionCore turned 10 matrix rows green (8 Technical + 2 Cost). Volume 2 reads “8/8 locked · 9/10 pages · ✓ Volume locked.”
sections.caption: Volumes locked; matrix satisfied; the Cost Volume built from a live-formula canvas.

sections.heading: Export your downloadables
body: With the volume locked, Download your deliverables. The Technical Volume exports to a submission-ready .docx (US-Letter, 1″ margins, the agency's fonts, figures inline and captioned). The Cost Volume exports to an .xlsx with live formulas.
Verified deliverables: a 10-page Technical Volume .docx (6 figures, 5 tables, all 8 DON TV2 sections) and a Cost Volume .xlsx — Base $199,502 ≤ $200k, Option $114,464 ≤ $115k, formulas live.
sections.caption: Page 1 of the exported Technical Volume — rendered by the system from your locked canvas.
